name: stab-and-silence
style: dry radio-play sound design, no music bed, no beat, no melody; shouted spoken dialogue only, each line answered by one isolated orchestral hit then dead air; solo violin sforzando stab, Bartok snap pizzicato, col legno crack of bow wood on strings, cello glissando sliding down into the floor; ambulance siren wailing and a racing heart monitor beep fill the gaps as sound effects; voices: a young woman screaming hoarse until her voice cracks, a panicked high-pitched male tenor, a gravel-throated older driver bellowing; then an elderly upper-class English aristocrat whining through glass, answered by one thin sour violin harmonic; ends on a continuous flat monitor tone, then total silence; close-miked, raw, claustrophobic, British TV hospital drama tension
exclude: singing, sung melody, chorus, rap, drum beat, groove, bassline, synth pad, sustained strings, piano, cheerful, comedic, upbeat, major key, epic trailer swell, choir, fade-in music, music after the flatline
lyrics:
[Spoken, shouted, no melody]
[Siren wailing, rain on the roof]

[Young woman, screaming, voice cracking]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!
[Violin stab, then silence]

[Young man, panicked, high]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!
[Snap pizzicato, monitor beeping fast]

[Driver, gravel voice, roaring]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!
[Col legno crack, brakes screech, siren cuts]

[Young man, bewildered]
Why have we stopped?!
[Low cello slides down]

[Old aristocrat, posh, petulant, muffled behind glass]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!
[Thin sour violin harmonic]

[Young woman, quiet, exhausted]
Fifty over twen—
[Flatline tone]
[Silence]
[End]
